arguments.text: 6000 m, 6 legs of 1000 m out-and-back. Hard start then settle to about critical power (pod ~151 W, boat ~89 W) through legs 1-5, aiming to finish with the pod reserve near empty. Hold even effort; compare same-direction legs to read current. Start final push around 800-1000 m to go if reserve allows (pod reserve above ~40%). Watch for anything slowing the boat at steady power (rudder weed, drag) via push_local and speed at same power. CP may be 10-25% off: check whether reserve trend matches how the paddler feels.

arguments.message: Boat slower than pod power plus current predicts: possible weed, drag or pod problem

arguments.text: Good start. Settle into race rhythm now.

text: Set plan and watches for drag and pod reserve; cued settle to about 163 s/500 after hard start; wake in 75 s to check.

arguments.text: Ease a little more. Long smooth strokes, save it for later.

Trust pod. Re-cued ease to 159 s/500 over ground at 2.4 min.

Cued ease to 178 s/500 over ground. If paddler still hurting at or below CP later, consider pod CP lower than 151.

text: Cued ease with no pace target: pod 164 W over sustainable 154 and paddler cooked; earlier pace target was pulling power up into the head current.

6000 m, 6 legs of 1000 m out-and-back (north legs 1,3,5 with about +0.25 m/s current; south legs 2,4,6 against it). Trust the pod (boat reserve over-reads early because push estimate lags). Hold pod power at sustainable (about 153 W, CP 151) legs 2-5; no ground-pace targets (they pull power up into the head current). Paddler said cooked at 6 min (8/10) with pod reserve 30-35%: reassure, keep even. If pod power drops well below CP without a cue, reserve may be emptier than modelled (CP too high): then lower cp_shaft. Final push from about 800-1000 m to go if pod reserve allows. Watch for drag incidents (push_local vs leg history).

text: Reassured the paddler: pod power at sustainable and slow GPS speed is the head current; updated plan.

arguments.text: Ease back a little. Even, steady strokes to the turn.

arguments.text: 9.8 min radio from escort: wind filling in from the north, 8-12 kt. Means headwind on north legs (3,5) against the helping current, tailwind on south legs (4,6) against the head current. Headwind of 10 kt adds a lot of air drag at OC1 speed, so north legs will be slower than leg 1. Check on leg 3 with legs(): leg 1 north had push_local about +0.25. Boat-model numbers will read wind as the paddler: keep trusting pod. Slightly more effort into headwind, slightly less with tailwind is the better split, but only if reserve allows (now 18%).

text: no cue: gate closed 20 s; noted the north wind report for leg 3; scheduled wake-up at 10.8 min handles pacing.

Pod reserve 13%, sustainable 152 W: on target now after the turn cue. Paddler again 8/10 hurting, not sure can hold (same words as 5.5 min). Reassure cue at 8.0 made power rise, so avoid reassure while on target. Even power across legs; watches will wake me on drift.

Letting it rebuild for the finish rather than pushing a paddler who keeps saying it hurts. Finish plan: last leg (6000-7000 m) is north into the headwind, the best place to spend the reserve; push or finish cue from about 1000 m if the reserve is above 15-20%.
